edges.demand: A convex body of affine dimension k holds at most k!·vol + k lattice points.
A gradient of an arithmetic circuit takes constant work per circuit operation.
A basis of a saturated lattice extends to an ambient unimodular basis. Minkowski’s second theorem and Mahler’s basis bound give the basis norm product bounds h, 2h and 9h at ranks one, two and three.
A symmetric convex body of volume 2^d·det contains a nonzero lattice point: the short multiple.
The symbolic game and real run agree until two values collide by lazy sampling of the label maps.
A nonzero polynomial of degree ≤d_f vanishes on the valid coin grid with probability at most d_f/(q−D).
Integer programs in dimension at most four take polynomial time.
Hermite form takes polynomial time with polynomial-size entries.

discharge.argument: The stated t_R holds under the same query caps.
The exact target and conditional recovery are stated.
The moments give the Jensen bound.
Same guess bound under the query cap.

add.label: Direct extraction and decryption
add.name: Extraction and decryption
add.statement: Every extractor output is ⊥ or a witness. In admissible extraction, at u=2Q+2, init and charged first marks cost at most ε_fΣ_s binom(L_s,2) and N_cmp(u)(θ+ε_f)+(binom(L+3u,2)+L+3u)ε_f. A target run has a first mark in {init, guess, charged, good}. For each b, good first marks with a kernel vector in their row space have probability ≤s_b+2ε_f, with s_b=B_b’s success on uniform Module-SIS. Good first marks with no such vector and no witness output have probability ≤2/q. For adversary time t and ≤Q_H queries per RO, both reductions take at most t+O(Q+d_RQ_H+μ)+poly(D,log q) in the prescribed model. On a witness and honest ciphertext the search target is Λ′=(r(w)−c_w)Ψ^α. For nonzero key weight, the search returning r(w)−c_w, or returning 0 with Ψ^α=0, gives K=[κ]_T. In the extractability experiment Pr[b′=b and Fail]≤1/2+(f_0+f_1)/4. Under (P5), E(2Q+2)≤(Q+1)/2^λ for integer 0≤Q<2^λ. For binary w with w_0=1 use k=1+wt(w). With either prescribed r,c_w, |r(w)−c_w|≤B throughout the support. The second moment is ≤(g√(k/12)+1/2)² for the independent sampler and ≤(g√((N+4)/48)+3/2)² for the centered sampler. A guess first mark has probability ≤Q_H/N_free≤2^λ/N_free for Q_H≤2^λ.
add.proof:
Inverse bound: under (I1)–(I6), v as in the lattice blob has a short multiple with x_0=0. Write ε=ε_tr and μ=μ_tr.

Trimming. For a lattice Θ of rank 1≤d≤3 with basis B, a centered box coordinate has moment generating function sinh(gt/2)/(g sinh(t/2)) by a geometric sum, with limit 1 at zero. Since sinh(x)/x≥1 and (2j+1)!≥6^jj!, this is at most exp(g²t²/24). Thus the centered image Y=Bᵀr_I−y_Θ satisfies E e^{uᵀY}≤e^{uᵀΣ_Θu/2} by independence. For Z=Σ_Θ^{−1/2}Y and an independent standard Gaussian G in dimension d, integrate e^{√(99/100)GᵀZ} in either order: E e^{99‖Z‖²/200}≤E e^{99‖G‖²/200}=10^d. Markov's inequality and (I2) bound the mass removed by 10^d e^{−99R_tr²/200}≤ε.

Integral facts. On a largest minor J, Cramer's rule bounds entries of B_iB_J^{−1} by one. Thus J is injective on the span and ‖y‖_∞≤‖y_J‖₁. For saturated Θ, a unimodular extension gives B an integral left inverse, so Bᵀ is onto. For rank-k Δ with k-minors of magnitude <q, a nonzero k-minor survives, making the k nonzero Smith entries in UΔV units mod q. A relation cᵀΔ≡0 mod q makes the first k entries of cᵀU^{−1} multiples of q. Zero them and multiply by U for the integral lift.

Prefixes. Place a largest minor J first. For k≥d factor the first k rows B_k=Y_kC_k, where Y_k bases the saturated prefix span. Its largest minor is J. Since Y_kᵀ is onto, h_k[Z^d:B_kᵀZ^k]=h(Θ). The cyclic enlargement on adding a row has order s_k=h_{k+1}/h_k. A fiber fixes the new coordinate modulo s_k, and each feasible coordinate contributes at most m_k/g because C_k is invertible. Thus m_{k+1}≤m_k⌈g/s_k⌉/g, with m_d=g^{−d}, h_d=1. At s_k≥g every fiber fixes the new coordinate.
For 1<s<g, the ratio is bounded by (1+s/g)/s≤s^{−1+1/b}: if s≥2^b use 1+s/g≤2; otherwise use concavity of s^{1/b}−1−s/2^b, zero at 2^b and nonnegative at 2 since ln(2)/b≥2^{1−b} for b≥7. For s=1 the ceiling factor is one. Hence m^b h^{b−1} is nonincreasing along such steps.
In rank three let r count ratios s_k>1. Their product is h, and telescoping the two products gives ∏(1/s_k+1/g)−1/h≤r(1/2+1/g)^{r−1}/g for r≥1, and zero for r=0. The bound peaks at r=2: the ratio at r=1 exceeds one and for r≥2 it is ≤(3/2)(1/2+1/g)<1. Thus m(Θ)≤g^{−3}ξ_tr(1/h+1/g). For m≥μ this yields h≤H_3 by (I2) and mh≤Γ_3/g³ by (I4).

Image count. Let rank-d Θ on |I|≤N trim nonempty F on I and i′, with d∈{1,2,3}. An image point of Φ(r)=(Bᵀr_I,r_{i′}) has mass ≤m(Θ)/g. For a full-dimensional image in an index-q coset project identically with k=d+1, δ=q, B_2=B, J=∅ and A=1.
Otherwise suppose F^⊥ has rank 1≤d′<d, largest minor J⊆I, with restrictions to I in span B. Then B_J contains the column span of Y_J for a normal basis Y, so has rank d′. Extend its integral kernel basis to a unimodular basis of Z^d, putting the kernel last. The changed B=(B_1,B_2) has (B_2)_J=0 and (B_1)_J invertible, and defines Φ without changing trimming. Its transpose (a,t)↦(Ba,t) identifies real normal spaces of Φ(F) and F by the restriction hypothesis. Thus k=dim Φ(F)=d+1−d′. Split the saturated image normal basis V into first d′ rows V_1 and the rest V_2. Pullback gives (B_1)_JV_1=Y_JC with C integral nonsingular, so Aδ≥h(F^⊥) for A=|det(B_1)_J| and δ=|det V_1|. Drop the first d′ coordinates, injectively on ker Vᵀ. The remaining differences satisfy V_2ᵀx≡0 mod V_1ᵀZ^{d′}, a subgroup of index δ by transpose surjectivity.
The projected hull is k-dimensional in an index-δ coset. A lattice simplex has edge determinant a nonzero multiple of δ, so vol≥δ/k!, so the lattice point bound is k!·vol/δ+k≤(k+1)!·vol/δ. The hull fits an interval of length ≤g times the projected ellipsoid of dimension j=k−1. Its volume is vol(Ball_j)(gR_tr/√12)^j√det(B_2ᵀB_2) by singular values, where Ball_j is the Euclidean unit ball. By Cauchy–Binet, A√det(B_2ᵀB_2)≤h(Θ)√binom(N,j), since (B_2)_J=0 makes each product minor a maximal minor of B. Using binom(N,j)≤N^j/j!,
Pr[F]·Aδ≤m(Θ)h(Θ)g^j R_tr^j N^{j/2}(j+2)!vol(Ball_j)/√(12^j j!).
For j=1,2,3 the last factor is 2√3, √2π or 20π/(9√2), respectively. By (I3) this gives Pr[F]≤Λ_d g^d h(Θ)m(Θ)/q, and otherwise Pr[F]h(F^⊥)≤Λ_{d−d′}g^{d−d′}h(Θ)m(Θ).

Regularization by descending rank: a saturated rank-d lattice with m≥μ+(3−d)ε has a regular extension losing ≤(3−d)ε. For d=3 the rank-three bound proves it. For d≤2 choose largest prefix fibers and trim each by R_{k−1} when defined, obtaining F_k of mass ≥m_k−ε≥μ+(2−d)ε. When F_k^⊥ strictly contains the saturated prefix Θ_k, it has rank e>d and e≤3 since Pr[F_k]>g^{−4}. Apply induction to it, obtaining regular R_k of mass ≥m_k−(3−d)ε. If R exists at the final prefix, use it.
Otherwise start at j+1 for the last j with R_j, or at d if none. Beyond that start F_{k+1}^⊥=Θ_{k+1}; s_k≥g would give the new unit normal, which vanishes on J, contradicting injectivity. Hence m_k^b h_k^{b−1} decreases. At d its value is g^{−db}≤μ(Γ_d/g^d)^{b−1} by (I4). At j+1 the second image count applies to R_j of rank e: F_{j+1} has normal Θ_{j+1} with largest minor J and restrictions in span Θ_j⊆span R_j. It gives Pr[F_{j+1}]h_{j+1}≤Λ_{e−d}Γ_e/g^d. By (I4), m_{j+1}≤A_inv Pr[F_{j+1}], and m_{j+1}≤m_j≤Pr[F_j]+ε≤g^{−d−1}+ε≤μP_d^{b−1}. Their product in m_{j+1}(m_{j+1}h_{j+1})^{b−1} gives ≤μ(Γ_d/g^d)^{b−1} since A_invΛ_{e−d}Γ_eP_d≤Γ_d. Finally m≥μ yields regularity.

Support induction. Place the m nonzero coordinates first, omitting coordinate zero. By the lattice blob p_i=gp(v_{[i]}ᵀ) satisfies θ<p_i≤1/g. Maintain a regular saturated Θ, rank d≤3, with v_{[i]} in its reduction, with m(Θ)≥p_i−3ε>μ. At i=1 use Z with h=1, m=1/g and Γ_1≥1 by (I4). At each step h≤H_d by regularity or the rank-three bound.
On the dominant-minor projection with determinant h, Minkowski II with ℓ₁ ball volume 2^d/d! gives minima product ≤d!h. Mahler bounds the basis lengths by λ₁,λ₂,3λ₃/2 as present. The coordinate bound lifts this basis with ∏‖B_j‖_∞≤a_d h for a_d=1,2,9. Write v_{[i]}≡Bc′ and c=(c′,v_{i+1}). Trim a maximal modular fiber cᵀΦ=t, obtaining F of mass ≥p_{i+1}−ε>μ. Since v_{i+1}≠0, the image lies in an index-q coset. Full dimension would give Pr[F]≤Λ_dΓ_d/q<μ by (I5) and the image count.
The image difference matrix Δ has rank k≤d. The ellipsoid diameter bounds each moment row by 2R_tr√[(Σ_Θ)_{jj}]≤T_tr‖B_j‖_∞ by Cauchy–Schwarz, and the last row by g−1≤T_tr. Using these bounds (all ≥1 with T_tr for the last row), each k-minor is ≤d!a_dH_dT_tr^d<q in magnitude by (I5). Lift cᵀΔ≡0 integrally and pull back by Φᵀ. The resulting normal reduces to v_{[i+1]}. The normal lattice has rank 1 to 3 by nonzeroness and the fiber bound, and maximum fiber mass ≥Pr[F]>θ−ε≥μ+2ε. Regularize, losing ≤2ε.
Finally Bz_0≡v_{[m]}≠0. The preimage in Z^d of the residue line of z_0 has index q^{d−1}; project it to J for determinant hq^{d−1}. By (I6) and integral h, d!hq^{d−1}≤β^d. The ℓ₁ ball of radius β therefore meets Minkowski's threshold. A nonzero projected point B_Jz lifts to 0<‖Bz‖_∞≤‖B_Jz‖₁≤β<q. Its residue is a nonzero multiple, and zero padding and inverse relabeling give x_0=0.

Lifting algorithm for nonzero v with v_0=0, 2β<q and 24β⁴<q³. Omit coordinate 0, permute and scale v to v_1=1. Four box points in the integer prefix lattice x_j≡v_jx_1 mod q have every four-row minor divisible by q³ by eliminating three columns modulo q using a nonzero residue column, or all columns vanish modulo q; their magnitudes ≤24β⁴<q³ make them zero. Thus the bounded span has dimension ≤3. From the previous bounded span S, initially zero, all new box points lie in S×R. Intersect this space with the prefix lattice by adjoining integer slack z_j in x_j−v_jx_1=qz_j to integer equations for S. For this equation matrix A use top-first column Hermite form on [A;I]. The nonzero upper blocks are independent by their distinct pivots; hence the other columns form a kernel basis in the lower block of this unimodular column transform. Project off the unique slacks, giving a lattice basis of rank ≤4. Rational elimination and the Hermite bound give polynomial bit sizes since S is stored by bounded independent points. In basis coordinates use integer programs for the box and either sign of each integral annihilator basis functional of the currently found span, requiring value ≥1 or ≤−1. If none succeeds the span is complete; each success grows it. Iterate prefixes. Return any nonzero final point, undoing the permutation and adding zero at coordinate 0. It cannot reduce to zero by β<q. If none was found, none exists. There are constantly many programs per prefix in dimension ≤4, so time is polynomial.

For symmetric W, the linked QAP facts make the coset sums of R_W the constraint tests, so R_W is allowed exactly when these pass. On roots of Z the numerator P_W−Z_0R_W vanishes except at d_j, where its values are the Booleanity tests. At ρ it equals W_{00}, so subtract W_{00}L_ρ for key division. Conversely either division forces R=R_W on cosets and then all tests by evaluation. Numerator degree ≤2D−2 and divisor degree ≥D−1 give quotient degree <D. A witness passes with W=wwᵀ and W_{00}=1.

Degree count. ϖ=Ω_{22}ζζ′ζ″ε clears all denominators. First-group degrees are ≤a=max(D+2K_1,Δ) from F (deg π_{k_1}≤2K_1), powers (Δ′≤D) and Y. For ϖ times the second-group exponents including α, H and search are bounded by max(D+n−1,2n−1)+6≤D+n+5 using k_leg≤n−1, deg z<n and deg A_i,B_i<D; the Ω pole offsets its linear numerator. Quotient and remainder degrees are ≤D+n+6+(J−1)Δ and N+n+9+(J′−1)Δ′: use deg γ_c=k_c+3, deg Z_c≤D−1 except k_key=0, deg Z_0=N+2, and subtract the ζ or ζ′ denominator. Cancellation has degree ≤2n+6 from deg(π η_a)=2, υ-degree ≤2n−2, at most one ε, and ζ″ below. The common bound is b=D+n+7+(J−1)Δ since (J′−1)Δ′≤D−N−2. The cleared κ,ακ terms have degrees D+7,D+8. Pairings have degree ≤a+b, and source differences ≤a+5 or b. All are ≤d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6 since a+b≤2D+2n+7+max(D+2K_1−Δ,0) by (P1), Δ≥1.

At fixed r the cleared target difference has degree ≤d_f. The valid grid has each side ≥q−D and no zero denominator. As ε_f=(d_f+61)/(q−D)<1, q−D>d_f. Schwartz–Zippel bounds nonidentity coincidences by ε_f and converts grid identities into rational identities.
At a fixed-r identity put a=Ω_{12}, b=Ω_{22}. Multiply by b, set b=0 and clear the other denominators, independent of a,b. Only H has a pole. Substitute y=B(τ)+t e_j; the t coefficient uses only the two j-poles, whose numerators are α_s s_leg(B_j−y_j) times −a and 1. Hence Σ_{s,leg}α_s s_leg(L_2−aL_1)=0, where L_m is the coefficient-weighted first-group exponent sum against H_m at b=0,y=B(τ).
The first-group types there are 1, ζτ^k, ζ′τ^k, ζ″B_i, π_{k_1}B_i and aπ_{k_1}B_i. Their weighted sums separate by sector α_s and type, with powers of τ independent and B_i independent by B(d_i)=e_i. Without π, s_X υ^{k_leg} distinguishes legs; with π the ε-free terms π s_X υ^{k_c} distinguish cells. Degree two in a kills all F_2,H_1 coefficients. Degree one kills every remaining H_1 coefficient except F_1, matching each F_1,H_1 with its F_2,H_2 coefficient.
In each sector take class π in the multigrading by π, Ω (jointly a,b), ζ, ζ′, ζ″. Matched F,H matrices cancel their hidden bases. The other pairs are F_1 with search bases or G_2 and the three power blocks with the quotient, remainder and cancellation bases. Dividing by α_s, the factor table gives Σ_c γ_c b_c+Φ=χ_sκ, where χ_plain=χ, χ_α=−D_K and
b_c=yᵀ(W_c r−u_c)+yᵀ(W_c−W_cᵀ)A(τ)+(P_{W_c}+h_c Z_c+Z_0 R_c)(τ).
The power blocks give h_c and allowed R_c. Each b_c is independent of ε,υ,s_X; Φ comprises masks, G_2 and cancellation pairs and has no s_X. Coefficients at ε⁰s_X υ^{k_c} give b_key=χ_s L_ρ, all other b_c=0 and then Φ=0. The y-linear part gives W_c r=u_c at d_0 since A(d_0)=0, and A(ρ)=e_0 and A(d_j)=e_j−e_0 make the skew matrix kill a basis. The constant part is the quotient criterion with −h_c,−R_c; evaluation at ρ gives key corner χ_s. In Φ, take the ε-free η_a coefficient: it is πyᵀt_a(υ) plus πP(υ) times the tie-base contribution. Cancel π and compare y_i to get the ties.
Only the H_1 pairs vary with r, so Δr changes a sector by α_sΣ_cγ_c yᵀW_cΔr. Zero stacks thus extend the identity to all r and give χ=0 by the key corner. Conversely an all-r identity makes W_c r=u_c for all r, hence W_c=0. Use differences for formal equality. Pairing a source difference with the opposite generator gives a target expression of the same exponent and zero stacks, so if formally nonzero it is a nonidentity at each fixed r and obeys the coincidence bound.

First marks. For init, condition on r and sum the ε_f coincidence bound over formally distinct received same-group pairs. The symbolic and uniform-mask runs couple through the first evaluated collision. A charged first mark is neither init nor guess. A good collision then gives a difference mark (a fresh guess cannot cancel); when the target query comes first, a good recorded target gives a key mark, and no entry gives guess. Thus charged marks require bad comparisons. Target coverage follows from M4.
Fix the independent symbolic transcript. A comparison with guesses, at fixed r, has a nonconstant guess monomial with a nonzero scalar or formally nonzero source coefficient; the latter stays nonzero by the fixed-r source bound. After multiplying by ϖ of degree five, the guess-source, guess-guess and bare-guess terms have degrees ≤d_f+1,7,6. Independent uniform guess variables extend the grid, giving coincidence probability ≤(d_f+1)/(q−D)≤ε_f. Without guesses, nonidentities cost ε_f. For a bad target comparison its fixed-r identities require the fiber of the selected nonzero light stack (zero would imply formal equality and χ=0). This adds at most θ.
With ≤3 entries per call, all guess comparisons fit binom(L+3u,2)+L+3u. Without guesses a first collision pairs the result at call j with ≤L+3j−1 earlier entries, and target comparisons use ≤Q results plus two initial target entries. The count is ≤QL+3Q(Q+1)/2+2≤N_cmp(2Q+2). The union bound gives the charge.

Rank and reduction. Stack rows as M and take a column basis including 0 if nonzero. Fix nonpivot positive coordinates. The fiber prescribes each pivot residue, costing ≤1/g independently at positive pivots and ≤1/g at pivot 0 after conditioning on all positive coordinates. Thus gp(W)≤g^{−d}; heaviness and (P3) give g^{−d}>g^{−4}. Every row-space scalar image maps a largest fiber to one value, so gp(vᵀ)≥gp(W).

Uniform challenge seed blocks give the real law; independent private draws do not affect replies and may be sampled first.
At a good first mark the record invariant gives its expression up to formal equality, from the target record or the result minus the old record. Earlier privately tested target matches were formal equalities or would have marked. Thus a private disagreement detects the good difference if its nonzero cleared polynomial survives, which fails with probability ≤d_f/(q−D)≤ε_f.

Formal representatives agree in stacks and identity at the run's r. By the permitted H_1 pairs, the sector gradient is α_sΣ_{c,i}γ_c y_i W^s_{c,i}, with W^s_{c,i} the cell row i. An alpha mark has zero plain gradient. A nonzero functional on the row space yields after dividing by α_sπ a nonzero polynomial of degree ≤n+2: γ_c/π=s_X υ^{k_c}(1+εω^{2k_1}), and the ε-free monomials s_X υ^{k_c}y_i are distinct. For each fresh gradient choose a functional killing the prior span if proper. The chance of failing to extend is ≤(n+2)/(q−D), so three draws span except with probability ≤3(n+2)/(q−D)≤ε_f.
With detection and spanning, the sector order obtains a kernel vector v in the mark space if no earlier solution was found. Since z(v)=0, v_0=0, and gp(vᵀ)≥gp(W)>θ. Conditions (P3),(P4) give a short lift. Any such kernel lift has x_0≡0 and |x_0|≤β<q, so x_0=0. Packing its remaining coefficients with zero padding gives positive norm ≤β and zero challenge image by the forms identity. The two private error bounds give s_b+2ε_f.

Witness existence for a nonzero usable rank-d stack, d≤3, without a kernel vector. Let U have a row-space basis as columns, u_j its transposed rows, and h_s=Uᵀσ^s(z) over K=F_{q^n}. The entries of h_0, hence h_a, are F_q-independent, where (a,b,c)=(n/2−1,n/2,n/2+1). A K-relation among h_{a+k}=h_a^{q^k}, k<d, gives a nonzero q-linear polynomial of degree ≤q^{d−1} vanishing on the q^d-element F_q-span of the entries of h_a, so h_a,h_b,h_c span K^d.
The U-weight, V-weight and conjugated U-weight assemblies are UM_sUᵀ for s=a,b,c, with symmetric M_s by a left inverse of U on both sides. The ties give M_s h_t=M_t h_s. Testing against spanning h_t makes every relation among h_s hold among M_s, so M_s=M(h_s) for a linear M. The ties and matrix symmetry make T(h,u,v)=uᵀM(h)v symmetric. Booleanity gives T(h,u_j,u_j−u_0)=0 for all h by spanning. Conjugacy gives M_a=σ^a(M_c), M_b=σ^b(M_b), since a+c=n and the V assembly is even.
If u_0=0, in a basis from the other rows T vanishes on repeats. Only d=3 allows a nonzero coefficient t on distinct indices. Each off-diagonal entry of M_s is t times the complementary coordinate of h_s. The two conjugacies imply t h_a=σ^a(t)h_0 and t h_b=σ^b(t)h_0. Thus t≠0 contradicts spanning, and T=0 contradicts the nonzero stack since coefficients of the U and V assemblies encode its cells.
Otherwise extend u_0 to a row basis. For binary δ of length d−1 take p_δ with coordinate pairings (1,δ) in that basis. Set w_δ=Up_δ and z_δ=z(w_δ)≠0. Basis triples reduce by Booleanity to subsets A of nonzero indices, replacing repeats by index zero. The cubes of pairing with p_δ are 1_{A⊆supp δ} on these triples, triangular with ones on the diagonal. They span T. Pairs also realize every A since d−1≤2, so the squares p_δp_δᵀ are independent. Thus M_s=Σ_δ c_δ σ^s(z_δ)p_δp_δᵀ. By square independence both conjugacies fix c_δ/z_δ under σ^a and σ^b, hence under σ. Write χ_δ=c_δ/z_δ∈F_q.
For each base-field passage test L, the assemblies pass by cellwise passage, linearity and conjugation. Therefore h_0ᵀQh_s=0 with Q=Σ_δ χ_δ L(w_δw_δᵀ)p_δp_δᵀ over F_q. Spanning and F_q-independence give Q=0. By square independence any δ with χ_δ≠0 passes every test. Such a δ exists by nonzeroness, and w_δ has corner one, hence is a witness.

Only checked witnesses are returned. The invariant represents a good difference by the tested difference. A good key record comes from a tested result: received target records have zero stacks and fresh guesses have a guess variable. Formal equality preserves sketches, so these mark-sector sketches were tested unless a witness was already returned.
The probe map (v_c)_c↦Σ_c W_c v_c surjects onto the row space V by symmetry. Hence three independent probes give uniform sketches in V, independent of the run through the mark. Their basis coordinate matrix has d≤3 independent uniform rows in F_q³, with rank loss probability ≤Σ_{j=0}^{d−1}q^{j−3}<2/q by sequential row tests. Otherwise the tested space is V and contains a witness. It has entry 1 at coordinate 0, then a pivot, and Boolean entries, so it is a candidate.

Timing. With V unused exponents and U undecided strings, the uniform remaining injection makes an undecided operand valid with probability V/U. Implement with one uniform integer in [1,U], accepting at ≤V and drawing uniformly outside assigned exponent keys. An unassigned result exponent gets a uniform undecided string; record a rejection on failure of the operand test. Memoize both map directions and rejects. Counters fit as the generator is assigned. Each call has ≤2 operand decisions and one result, plus constant table, name, circuit and private evaluation work. A name uses the eligibility flag and the label of the negation; missing records start at zero.
Install the seed challenge, then memoize each oracle miss in d_R field draws or one key-set draw, totaling O(d_R Q_H). Assign κ's label without a record and memoize its key answer. Message advice and masking cost O(μ). From O(DN) coefficient advice, the published formulas and input derivatives at all fixed points cost poly(D,log q): N,n≤D, JΔ≤D+n, J′Δ′≤D (J′=1 if empty), and k d_R<n. For each of ≤2 candidates the six reverse passes cost O(Q) plus polynomial input chain-rule work. Zero the other sector at the second pairing inputs; direct target terms have zero r-derivative. The kernel intersection, lift and packing are polynomial. Add t.

Honest Comb uses W_c=ξ_cwwᵀ, killing skew and giving r(w)ψ with ψ=y(w)Σ_c γ_cξ_c. The chunk pairings subtract the two quotient cases and allowed remainders, leaving ξ_keyκ. Each honest tie is w times the numerator of x_a^0; w_0=1 and tie divisibility make those divisions exact. The mask identity and coefficient ranges then cancel the entire mask. Thus Λ=[ξ_keyκ+r(w)ψ]_T. The first left coordinates paired with the leg scalars give Ψ=[ψ]_T; scaling second inputs multiplies both by α. Centering gives Λ′=(r(w)−c_w)Ψ^α. For nonzero weight the correct t cancels r(w)ψ in K. If Ψ^α=0 then Ψ=0 since α≠0, and t=0 suffices. Either gives K=[κ]_T.

In the common uniform-mask run the target event and off-target output are independent of b. If the target probability is p and its joint failure probability is f=(f_0+f_1)/2≤p, success with failure contributes at most (1−p)/2 off target and f on target, with total ≤1/2+f/2.

The quadratic coefficient of E is (θ+10ε_f)/2≥0. Its endpoints at 2 and 2^{λ+1} lie below u/2^{λ+1} by (P5), so convexity bounds it by that line throughout. Substitute u=2Q+2.

Search range. Let Y_i=r_i−m for the independent draws with m=(g+3)/2, including the star draw when centered. They have mean zero, variance (g²−1)/12 by summing squares and |Y_i|≤(g−1)/2. The deviation is a linear combination of these with coefficients a and rounding bounded by b. In the independent case the k selected coefficients are one and the fractional part of km is ≤1/2. In the centered case the star coefficient is one and the others w_i−1/2; subtracting the floor of s/2 for s=Σ_{i>0}r_i adds {s/2}, and the unrounded center contributes its fractional part. These total ≤3/2. Thus |r(w)−c_w|≤(g−1)‖a‖₁/2+b≤B, and its L² norm is ≤g‖a‖₂/√12+b by independence and the triangle inequality. The squared coefficient norms k and 1+N/4 give the bounds. Jensen gives the expected square root of the absolute deviation at most the fourth root of its second moment, hence O(√g N^{1/4}).

Guess marks. Use the full uniform-mask run with independent key answers. Given the exposed injection and other coins fixing the query, an unassigned target exponent has a uniform undecided label. Two received labels and at most three decisions per call leave ≥2^{ℓ_lab}−2−3Q≥N_free strings as Q<2^λ. Before a mark assigned labels have entries. A guess therefore needs a query hitting the target before assignment, with total probability ≤Q_H/N_free by the union bound and coupling.
